details.label: Discussion
details.text: Supercells and supercell hybrid clusters continue across portions of northern Illinois. As the low-level jet has strengthened, a few low topped supercells have shown weak rotation. One supercell in Lee County near the warm front/outflow boundary across northern Illinois approached 60 kft with more pronounced and long lived rotation and reports of a tornado. VAD profiles from KLOT are sampling 0-3 km SRH around 350-400 m2/s2, with weakening flow above 3 km. Given the favorable low-level shear, transient weak rotation will likely continue with low topped cells south of the boundary. Any storm that can anchor to the boundary may have potential for a tornado in the short term. Mode is becoming more clustered through time, with increasing damaging wind potential later into the overnight.
